llmlang.parser.parse.disposition: marked 7 grammar-rule bullets as # commentary (structural constraints on valid input - summary/data-marker placement, bullet nesting, test-bullet placement, hint parsing, @entry-point/→ call validity) instead of plain - bullets. These describe properties of the format, not steps parse() takes, so they read oddly as flat behavior bullets and would read worse if parse() ever becomes flow-reachable. No behavior changed - this adds # support to the parser/format and applies it here as the first real usage.

llmlang.extractor.extract_by_handle.disposition: marked the 'including the comment line itself means...' bullet as # commentary - it's a rationale for why code_hash is computed the way it is, not a step extract_by_handle performs. No behavior changed.

llmlang.flow.generate_flow.disposition: two additions: (1) a resolved → call line now renders with the target's full canonical name plus its own parenthesized summary, so a reader doesn't need to jump to the target's header to know what it does; (2) excludes # commentary bullets from rendering, the same treatment as ~ test bullets, since neither describes execution.

llmlang.flow.generate_flow_for_tree.disposition: bullets updated to describe the new # exclusion (mirrors the existing ~ exclusion, same rationale).

llmlang.lockfile_builder.build.disposition: marked 'has no notion of dispositions...' and 'reproduces the same hashes...' as # commentary - both are properties/guarantees about build() as a whole (a scope note contrasting it with finalize, and an idempotency guarantee across runs), not steps taken during one call. No behavior changed.

llmlang.lockfile_builder.finalize.disposition: marked 'builds every hash and disposition fresh from... never carries anything forward...' as # commentary - a statelessness guarantee, not a step. No behavior changed.
